# CamelBee Code Review

Review the codebase (or $ARGUMENTS if specified) for CamelBee anti-patterns and architecture violations.

**Important:** This microservice was generated by the CamelBee MCP Server and is fully working and tested out of the box. The existing generated code is the source of truth. Focus review on user-added or user-modified code — do NOT flag the original generated patterns as issues.

## Review Checklist

### 1. Route Architecture
- [ ] Every route calls `camelBeeRouteConfigurer.configureRoute(this)` first
- [ ] Consumer routes use `errorHandler(genericExceptionHandler.appErrorHandler())`
- [ ] Central and producer routes use `errorHandler(noErrorHandler())`
- [ ] Every route has `.routeId()`
- [ ] Every backend endpoint in central routes has `.id()`
- [ ] No direct backend calls from consumer routes (must go through central)
- [ ] Central routes store `Constants.ORIGINAL_BODY` before fan-out
- [ ] Producer routes store response in `Constants.ACTUAL_RESPONSE_BODY`

### 2. Model Layer Boundaries
- [ ] API models only in consumer routes and API mappers
- [ ] Domain models flow through central routes
- [ ] Infra models only in producer routes and infra mappers
- [ ] No cross-layer model usage (e.g., API model in producer route)

### 3. MapStruct Mappers
- [ ] All mappers use `@Mapper` with correct `componentModel` (spring/cdi)
- [ ] All mappers reference `SharedMapperConfig.class`
- [ ] No manual mapping code that should be in MapStruct
- [ ] Mapper tests exist for all mappers

### 4. Test Coverage
- [ ] Every central route has a unit test with AdviceWith mocks
- [ ] Every interface has integration tests with TestContainers
- [ ] Every HTTP-accessible interface has black-box tests
- [ ] Tests use `@ParameterizedTest` + `@MethodSource` for multi-format
- [ ] Test data producers exist for all model layers

### 5. Configuration
- [ ] No hardcoded URLs, ports, or credentials in Java code
- [ ] All external config uses `application.yml` with `${ENV_VAR:default}` pattern
- [ ] Docker Compose services match what the code expects
- [ ] Init scripts (SQL, topics, queues) are consistent with route config

### 6. Framework-Specific (check which framework)
- [ ] Correct DI annotations for the framework
- [ ] Correct marshaling approach (especially Quarkus JacksonDataFormat)
- [ ] Correct split expressions (Quarkus native: no lambdas)
- [ ] Quarkus: new model classes registered in `ReflectionConfig.java` for native builds

### 7. Security
- [ ] OAuth2/JWT routes validate tokens before processing (if OAuth enabled)
- [ ] No hardcoded credentials, API keys, or secrets in Java code or config
- [ ] Sensitive config uses environment variables, not hardcoded values
- [ ] Keycloak realm config matches application.yml security settings

### 8. Observability
- [ ] CamelBee tracer config preserved (`camelbee.*` properties)
- [ ] Logging uses SLF4J (not System.out/err)
- [ ] MDC fields not removed from logback-spring.xml
- [ ] Transaction ID propagation via `UuidResolver` not broken

### 9. Docker & Infrastructure
- [ ] Docker Compose services have health checks where applicable
- [ ] Init scripts (SQL, CQL, JS) match the domain model schema
- [ ] WireMock stubs match the backend API contracts
- [ ] Flyway migrations are consistent across database vendors

## Report Format

For each finding, report:
- **Severity**: Critical / Warning / Info
- **File**: path and line number
- **Issue**: what is wrong
- **Fix**: how to fix it
